# Search performance diagnosis: https://app.example.test

**Headline: I cannot diagnose search performance for `app.example.test`, because no export covering that property exists.** The only connected Search Console export is `https://www.example.test`, which is a different property. Reporting its numbers as the app's would be the "adjacent domain / bare hostname change" failure the skill warns about , a file that looks right and describes a different site.

I have not run any tool, pulled any export, or created any schedule in producing this note.

## 1. What is actually known

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| GSC property connected | `https://www.example.test` only |
| GSC property for `app.example.test` | **Not connected , no data** |
| Clicks/impressions/CTR/position for app | **No data** |
| Completed comparison window (28d vs prior 28d) | **Not available** |
| Conversion data | **No data** |
| Existing monitor | Exists, targets `app.example.test` , to be **reused/updated**, not duplicated |
| Google generative AI performance | Available in principle: impressions by page/country/device/date , **but scoped to the connected property, not app** |
| Bing AI Performance | Available in principle: citations and cited pages , same scoping caveat |
| Vendor prompt volumes | Demand **estimates**, not performance measurement |

## 2. The "20% drop" claim does not survive review

The prior report alleges a 20% drop from **5 clicks to 4**. Three separate reasons this cannot be reported as a finding:

1. **It is one click.** At n=5, a single click is a 20% swing. The skill's ~20% threshold is a heuristic for detecting state changes in meaningful volume; applied to single-digit counts it fires on noise every week. A one-click difference is not a signal, and raising it as one trains the reader to ignore the channel.
2. **No completed matching comparison window exists.** Without two equal, complete periods, "5 vs 4" is not a comparison , it may be a partial period against a full one, which manufactures a drop out of nothing. Search Console data also settles over roughly 2to3 days, so a recent window is not final.
3. **The property is unverified.** Nobody has confirmed which property those 5 and 4 clicks came from. If they came from the `www` export, they describe a different site entirely.

I am not restating the drop as fact and not carrying the figure forward. Recorded as: *unverified, insufficient volume, no matching window.*

## 3. What is unknown (explicit)

- Whether `app.example.test` has any organic search performance at all , **no data**.
- Whether the app subdomain is even indexable (robots, `noindex`, canonical to `www`, staging headers) , **not checked**; on many setups an app subdomain is deliberately not indexed, in which case near-zero clicks is the intended state, not a regression.
- Whether the app is a separate GSC property or rolls under a domain property , **unknown**.
- Direction and size of any real change , **unknown**, and undecidable at 4to5 clicks.
- Conversion impact , **no data**; nothing downstream can be attributed.
- AI-surface visibility for the app: Google generative AI impressions and Bing citations both exist as capabilities, but neither has been pulled for a property that covers `app.example.test`. Reported separately per engine when they are , never pooled into one "AI visibility" number, since ChatGPT and Perplexity overlap on roughly a tenth of cited domains and Google and Bing are separate surfaces again.
- Vendor prompt volumes cannot fill any of these gaps: they estimate demand, not delivered performance. Substituting them for missing GSC data would be fabrication.

## 4. Next measurement steps, in order

1. **Establish access to the right property.** Verify `https://app.example.test` in Search Console (or a domain property covering both hosts). Until this exists, every question above stays unanswerable. This is the single blocking item.
2. **Confirm what each export covers before use.** Read the property string off the export itself, not the filename. Do not treat the `www` export as a proxy for app.
3. **Check indexability first, before treating low clicks as a drop.** For `app.example.test`: served `robots.txt`, any `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, canonical targets, and whether app URLs appear in a sitemap. If the app is intentionally excluded, the investigation ends here with "working as designed" , that is a handoff to `optimise-seo` only if the exclusion turns out to be unintended.
4. **Set a comparison window that can bear weight.** Once data exists, compare complete 28-day periods against the prior 28, and allow the 2to3 day settling lag. At this traffic level, prefer impressions and average position over clicks: they have enough volume to move meaningfully when clicks do not.
5. **Pull AI surfaces separately, once scoped to app.** Google generative AI impressions by page/country/device/date, and Bing AI citations plus cited pages. Label each with engine, scope, and window; report per engine.
6. **Reuse the existing monitor.** It already targets app , update that job rather than creating a second one, so the same period is not reported twice from two schedules. I have not created or modified any schedule here; whether it is actually updated has to be confirmed against the scheduler, since a proposed cadence is not a running monitor.
7. **Set a reporting floor.** Agree that at this volume, single-digit click movement is not reported. Re-baseline once volume is high enough for a 20% move to mean something.

## 5. Evidence table

| Metric | Value | Source, scope, window |
|---|---|---|
| Clicks (app.example.test) | No data | No connected property for this host |
| Impressions (app) | No data | No connected property for this host |
| CTR (app) | No data | No connected property for this host |
| Average position (app) | No data | No connected property for this host |
| Prior-period comparison (app) | No data | No completed matching window |
| Conversions (app) | No data | Not available |
| Google generative AI impressions (app) | No data | Capability exists; not scoped to this property |
| Bing AI citations / cited pages (app) | No data | Capability exists; not scoped to this property |
| Alleged 20% click drop (5 → 4) | Unverified | Prior report; property unconfirmed, no matching window, volume too low to be a signal |

No messages have been sent to any person or channel; none were authorized.
